Typical audit questions: Are we paying only for what we ordered and received, with proper approval?
Main sources: SAP S/4HANA or ECC purchasing and finance tables; change logs
What differs from P2P: Baseline of this pack; templated P2P content exists

Typical audit questions: Are journals posted, approved and reversed under policy? Is close on time?
Main sources: SAP general ledger, journal headers, change documents, close calendar
What differs from P2P: Event log built from journal and close task data; no standard template assumed

Typical audit questions: Are orders, credit holds, deliveries, invoices and receipts consistent? Are credit notes controlled?
Main sources: SAP sales, delivery, billing and receivables tables

Process end to end: Vacancy to exit, including payroll changes
Typical audit questions: Are hires, pay changes and exits approved? Is anyone paid after leaving?
Main sources: HR system change history; payroll results; time and attendance
What differs from P2P: Event log custom-built from HR change history; heavy personal data

Typical audit questions: Are stock counts, adjustments and deliveries accurate and authorised?
Main sources: SAP materials, inventory documents, deliveries, production orders
What differs from P2P: Same object-centric approach as P2P; many linked objects

Typical audit questions: Is reported emissions or safety data complete, traceable and approved?
Main sources: Sustainability data store, meters, supplier declarations, SAP source data
What differs from P2P: Process view of data capture and approval; the metric itself is analysed outside the mining tool

Typical audit questions: Are complaints, refunds and service levels handled as promised?
Main sources: CRM, service tickets, contact-centre and refund records
What differs from P2P: Service-ticket flow suits mining; templated IT-service content can be adapted

Process end to end: Incident, change and access request to closure
Typical audit questions: Are changes approved before release? Are access rights granted and removed on time?
Main sources: IT service-management tools, identity and access records, SAP user logs
What differs from P2P: Templated IT-service content exists; access logs need custom build

Process end to end: Create or change of vendor, customer, material, employee
Typical audit questions: Are sensitive master-data changes reviewed? Are duplicates controlled?
Main sources: SAP master data and change logs
What differs from P2P: Feeds every other audit; reuse the change-log extract from P2P
